prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Green Party Manifesto 2024 (ideology-neutral)

- Health and care
  - NHS: reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access (same-day for urgent need); universal NHS dentistry via new contract; expand community diagnostics; mental health therapies within 28 days; National Cancer Plan; end new HIV transmissions by 2030.
  - Workforce and capital: pay restoration for staff (including junior doctors); additional NHS revenue funding rising to c. £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years; £1.5bn extra for public health; primary care: +£1.5bn/yr by 2030 and £2bn capital.
  - Social care: free personal care; national career/pay structure; £20bn/yr investment; “Gloria’s Law” right to an essential care supporter.
  - Disabled people: 5% uplift to disability benefits; oppose voucherisation of PIP; free SEND transport 16–18; workplace support.
  - Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; guaranteed counselling; extended “staying put.”

- Housing and planning
  - 150,000 new social homes per year; end Right to Buy; local rent controls; end no-fault evictions.
  - Building standards: Passivhaus-equivalent for new homes; solar/low‑carbon heating mandated; MEES to EPC C; planning reforms to align homes with services and protect green spaces.
  - Retrofit/adaptation: £29bn for home insulation (to EPC B), £9bn for low‑carbon heat, £4bn for public buildings, £7bn for heat‑risk adaptation; area-based delivery; powers to bring empty homes into use; tenancy boards for dispute resolution.

- Energy and climate
  - No new oil/gas licences; rising carbon tax; community ownership thresholds; end de‑facto ban on onshore wind; Local Electricity Bill.
  - Generation targets: by 2035—80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, 100GW solar; wind ~70% of electricity by 2030.
  - Grid/storage: major grid expansion, offshore meshing, more interconnectors and storage; green hydrogen for industry.
  - Bioenergy: end imported biomass subsidies; stricter sustainability rules.
  - Nuclear: stop new projects; plan to phase out existing plants.

- Economy, tax and investment
  - Public/green investment averaging £40bn/yr across power, buildings, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water and sewage.
  - Public ownership: rail, water companies, Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
  - Finance: BoE mandate to support transition; bank/lender fossil divestment by 2030; FCA action on fossil listings; regional mutual banks (+£10bn capital) and £2bn/yr local decarb grants; Prompt Payment Code in law.
  - Tax changes: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance reliefs; council tax revaluation; carbon tax £120/t rising toward £500/t; windfall taxes; VAT shifts. Borrowing to invest; savings from cancelling Trident.

- Work and incomes
  - Charter of Workers’ Rights; repeal recent anti‑union laws.
  - Minimum wage £15/h (support for SMEs via higher Employment Allowance); 10:1 pay ratio; day‑one rights; tribunal fees abolished; equal pay audits; full rights for platform workers; move toward shorter working week.
  - Social security: +£40/week to UC/legacy benefits; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; disability benefits +5%; carers +10%/month; pensions uprated; end sanctions; long‑term UBI goal.

- Nature, animals, food
  - Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; DEFRA +£1.5bn; public ownership of water; Clean Air Act; peatland rewetting, woodland/scrub/urban biodiversity.
  - Animal protection commission; ban blood sports; phase out cages/factory farming practices; ban lead ammo/snaring.
  - Farming: nearly triple support to transition to nature‑friendly production; reduce pesticides; boost horticulture and local food networks; free daily school meals and breakfast clubs to Year 6; food education.

- Education
  - Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings/RAAC; curriculum/assessment reform; Natural History GCSE; bring academies under LAs; VAT and end charitable status for private schools (SEN exempt); SEND +£5bn; nurses and counsellors in schools.
  - Early years: £1.4bn/yr for Sure Start; 35 hours childcare from 9 months.
  - FE/HE: +£3bn to sixth forms; £12bn lifelong learning; restore EMA; scrap HE tuition fees and restore grants; address graduate debt long‑term.

- Transport
  - Public transport subsidies to £10bn/yr; £19bn over five years for networks, electrification, cycling/walking; rail to public ownership; £2.5bn/yr for active travel.
  - Roads/EVs: oppose new roads; road pricing; restore fuel‑duty escalator; end new ICE sales by 2027; phase-out use by 2035; EV scrappage up to £5bn/yr; 20mph default in built‑up areas; heavier vehicles pay more VED; more rail freight.
  - Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3h; apply carbon tax to kerosene; no airport expansion; reskilling support.

- Democracy, rights, migration
  - Fair Politics Act: proportional representation; repeal voter‑ID rules; stricter lobbying/think‑tank transparency; party funding reform; votes at 16; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; +£5bn/yr for English local government.
  - Human rights: retain HRA/ECHR access; restore legal aid; scrap Prevent; trans self‑ID; X passport option.
  - Migration/asylum: end hostile environment and NRPF; safe routes; right to work while claims decided; abolish minimum income rules for spouses; restructure Home Office into Department of Migration; fees at cost; NHS access for visa holders.

- Arts, media, digital
  - £5bn over five years for community sport/arts/culture; protect venues/night-time economy; VAT exemption for cultural events; local media grants; media ownership cap (20%); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation; creator IP protection.

- Justice and policing
  - Community policing; end routine stop and search and facial recognition; restorative justice with presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; invest in MoJ (legal aid, courts, judges); national strategy on violence against women/girls; decriminalise sex work; youth services funding; drug policy reform with decriminalised personal possession and health-led diversion.

- Foreign policy and security
  - Support Ukraine; work toward EU re‑entry (customs union, free movement, Erasmus as steps); Israel‑Palestine: immediate ceasefire, recognise Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, support war‑crimes investigations.
  - Aid/climate finance: ODA to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; Loss & Damage contributions; debt relief; anti‑ecocide efforts; reparatory justice inquiry.
  - Trade: remove ISDS‑type mechanisms; uphold labour, environmental and animal standards.
  - Nuclear/NATO: sign TPNW, cancel Trident and dismantle UK nuclear arsenal; remain in NATO while advocating no‑first‑use and greater emphasis on diplomacy.
